conditions.description: Participation restricted to legal entities established in EU Member States, Iceland, Norway, and associated countries: Canada, Israel, Republic of Korea, New Zealand, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.
Entities controlled by non-eligible countries may be excluded from participation unless sufficient guarantees are provided.
Activities are expected to start at TRL 2 and achieve TRL 5 by the end of the project.
Maximum EU contribution per project is €19,000,000; both the minimum and maximum expected EU contribution are €19,000,000 (fixed amount).

Portfolio coverage procedure: grants will be awarded to ensure at least one funded project focuses on each of the three sectors — healthcare, advanced manufacturing, and in-vehicle autonomous driving — subject to proposals passing all evaluation thresholds.
Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) financial ceilings: maximum €300,000 per grant at stage 2; maximum €2,250,000 per grant at stage 3; maximum €2,550,000 per third party.
Standard Horizon Europe RIA minimum consortium requirements apply: at least 3 independent legal entities from 3 different eligible countries.
conditions.assumption_note: Standard Horizon Europe RIA minimum consortium requirement per General Annex B; not explicitly stated in the topic-specific call extract documents. The topic source documents are silent on minimum consortium size and composition requirements beyond geographic eligibility restrictions. Verification against General Annex B is required.

conditions.description: Open access requirements apply to research results and publications produced under this grant, consistent with Horizon Europe open science obligations.
conditions.assumption_note: Standard Horizon Europe open access mandate per the Programme Guide and General Annex F; not explicitly stated in the topic-specific call extract documents. The topic requirement to share communicable results via the AI-on-demand platform (call_entry.scope field of HORIZON-CL4-2026-05-DIGITAL-EMERGING-02.slice.json) implies open sharing obligations, but the full open access mandate derives from the normative framework (Tier 1), not this Tier 2B source.
